name: Khaki Brown
lede: Khaki Brown is a dark olive-brown, named from the dust-colored cloth of army uniforms.

sections.title: Dust-colored cloth
sections.body:
Khaki is a Hindi word meaning dust-colored, and Paterson says it was the term for the fabric of British army field uniforms [1]. During the First World War the British dye industry, then small, scrambled to supply it: one firm, Read Holliday, sold both a khaki yellow and a khaki brown [2]. Garfield's source says the shortage was so great that dyers could earn more selling dye than using it [2].

The swatch here is from the xkcd color survey of 2010, and ISCC-NBS would call it light olive [3]. It sits near [[khaki]], [[olive]] and [[drab]] [1][3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Khaki Brown is uncommon in paintings: 89 of 23,781, 0.4 per cent [4]. It is mostly an accent and peaks in the 1900s, at 1.6 times the expected rate [4]. Its first match in the archive is a painting of 1505, 505 years before the swatch's record: a look-alike hue in an aged photograph [4].

questions.q: What does khaki mean in Hindi?
True or false: a British firm sold khaki brown dye during the First World War.

openers: Khaki means dust-colored in Hindi, and WWI dyers sold both khaki yellow and khaki brown.
